deadline_definition: Backend recovery starts immediately before restoration is requested and includes startup/readiness; R18 starts after confirmed worker death and includes natural lease expiry. Browser recovery starts at the observed transport fault, or resume request for R07/R08; R09 starts at the first actual expired-URL 403. A timed out, skipped, missing, or individually rerun case fails its full pass.
common_invariants: Intended fault is directly observed, not inferred solely from READY.
Recovered status is READY with exact source/worker/download byte count and SHA-256.
One logical file and one final storage object; no leaked multipart session.
Download access is denied before verification and for a different workspace.
Fault control and cleanup affect only this disposable test project.

cases.name: Lost upload initiation reply
cases.fault_boundary: After initiation commits, before browser receives reply
cases.expected_recovery: Reselecting the original file reuses the same request ID and logical upload.

cases.name: Lost part-signing reply
cases.fault_boundary: After signing transaction commits, before browser receives reply
cases.expected_recovery: Re-signing retains the checksum and multipart session.

cases.name: Interrupted part PUT before acceptance
cases.fault_boundary: Browser storage PUT is interrupted before the complete part is accepted
cases.expected_recovery: Only the interrupted part needs transfer; acknowledged parts remain confirmed.

cases.name: Lost accepted PUT reply
cases.fault_boundary: Storage accepts a complete PUT, then its reply is discarded
cases.expected_recovery: Re-signing reconciles accepted bytes without another PUT for that part.

cases.name: Lost acknowledgement request
cases.fault_boundary: Part PUT succeeds; acknowledgement is discarded before reaching API
cases.expected_recovery: Re-signing discovers the accepted storage part and continues.

cases.name: Lost committed acknowledgement reply
cases.fault_boundary: Acknowledgement commits, then its reply is discarded
cases.expected_recovery: Retry/resume preserves the confirmed receipt without resending bytes.

cases.name: Browser reload after confirmed parts
cases.fault_boundary: Several parts are acknowledged before browser reload
cases.expected_recovery: Same-file reselection sends only missing parts.

cases.name: Pause while parts are in flight
cases.fault_boundary: A storage PUT is active when the user pauses
cases.expected_recovery: Resume reconciles accepted parts and safely transfers missing bytes.

cases.name: Expired signed part URL
cases.fault_boundary: A genuinely expired S3-compatible signature is used before PUT
cases.expected_recovery: Storage rejects the expired URL; a fresh signature continues the same multipart session.

cases.name: API hard kill during upload
cases.fault_boundary: API process is killed during an incomplete multipart session
cases.expected_recovery: Restarted API retains session and acknowledged receipts.

cases.name: API hard kill after completion intent
cases.fault_boundary: Durable FINALIZING intent commits before storage completion
cases.expected_recovery: Reconciler completes the stored manifest.

cases.name: Lost storage completion reply
cases.fault_boundary: Storage accepts multipart completion but its response is lost
cases.expected_recovery: Recovery validates existing object identity/length and reaches processing.

cases.name: Database transaction failure after storage completion
cases.fault_boundary: Storage completed; processing/outbox transaction fails before commit
cases.expected_recovery: Retry uses existing object and durably records outbox work.

cases.name: Lost committed completion reply
cases.fault_boundary: PROCESSING and outbox commit before API reply is lost
cases.expected_recovery: Repeated completion returns existing state without duplicate logical effects.

cases.name: Redis outage before publication
cases.fault_boundary: Redis is unavailable before dispatcher publishes durable outbox work
cases.expected_recovery: Outbox survives and processing resumes after Redis restoration.

cases.name: Dispatcher hard kill after publication
cases.fault_boundary: Actual broker publication succeeds before outbox deletion commits
cases.expected_recovery: Uncommitted outbox survives; duplicate delivery is harmless.

cases.name: Lost published broker message
cases.fault_boundary: A published broker message is removed before worker delivery
cases.expected_recovery: Database reconciliation republishes missing processing work.

cases.name: Worker hard kill during verification
cases.fault_boundary: Worker is killed after streaming some source bytes while holding a live claim
cases.expected_recovery: Natural lease expiration permits a new worker to stream and verify the original object.

cases.name: PostgreSQL outage at worker final transaction
cases.fault_boundary: PostgreSQL is unavailable when worker writes the verification result
cases.expected_recovery: Durable processing survives; recovery eventually commits the correct result.

cases.name: Storage disconnect during worker streaming
cases.fault_boundary: Storage becomes unavailable after worker consumes some source bytes
cases.expected_recovery: Retry opens a new complete source stream and verifies all bytes.
